section_summary: This section documents relief activity involving Japan from 1945 through 1949, including Brazilian fundraising, Red Cross shipments, parcel and remittance regulations, foreign-sponsored welfare projects, and the disposition of hospitals created after the 1923 earthquake. It also records Japan’s formal gratitude to overseas Japanese communities for postwar aid and diplomatic efforts to circulate that resolution throughout the Americas. The final documents concern flood-control policy, wartime prisoner-of-war relief shipments, and American Red Cross personnel and finances in East Asia.

subfiles.title: Letter concerning Brazilian funds for relief in Japan
subfiles.from: Edward B. Peacock, Licensed Agencies for Relief in Asia
subfiles.to: Allan Dawson, Division of Brazilian Affairs, Department of State
subfiles.about: Requests advice on transferring Brazilian-raised relief funds to the United States for purchasing and shipping supplies to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Peacock reports Akira Ohtani's Japan Relief Committee in Rio can't remit funds to LARA and argues American purchases would use them better since Brazilian supplies are limited, expensive and costly to ship.

subfiles.title: Reply on Brazilian foreign-exchange restrictions
subfiles.from: Allan Dawson, Division of Brazilian Affairs, Department of State
subfiles.to: Edward B. Peacock, Licensed Agencies for Relief in Asia
subfiles.about: Explains why Brazilian relief funds cannot readily be remitted to the United States and suggests purchasing Brazilian goods instead.
subfiles.summary: Dawson explains that the Bank of Brazil allocates scarce dollar exchange by priority categories and that charitable remittances fall into the lowest category. Since approval may be delayed indefinitely, he suggests converting the cruzeiro funds into Brazilian products acceptable for relief work in Japan.

subfiles.title: American Red Cross letter on Chinese Red Cross supplies sent to Japan
subfiles.from: Philip H. Ryan, American National Red Cross
subfiles.to: William M. McCahon, Department of State
subfiles.about: Provides the Chinese Red Cross explanation for sending American Red Cross supplies to the Japanese Red Cross after an earthquake.
subfiles.summary: Chinese Red Cross's secretary-general says wartime American supplies came with broad authority to redistribute them, apologizes for any breach in aiding the Japanese Red Cross, and Ryan recommends closing the issue.

subfiles.title: Inquiry about gift parcels and assistance to a Christian school in Japan
subfiles.from: R. C. Neuendorffer
subfiles.about: Asks about charges on gift packages sent to Japanese recipients and ways to support a Christian school in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Poorly reproduced letter asks whether Japan imposes duty on gift packages and whether money can be sent to help a Christian school in Japan.

subfiles.title: Reply concerning relief parcels and monetary gifts to Japan
subfiles.from: Frank A. Schuler Jr., Department of State
subfiles.about: Explains parcel limits, prohibited goods, and alternatives for sending financial assistance to a Japanese Christian school.
subfiles.summary: Schuler says relief parcels are duty-free apart from a possible eight-yen clearance charge, gives weight and content limits, and, since postal remittances are banned and bank transfers use an unfavorable rate, recommends giving through denominational mission boards.

subfiles.title: Internal memorandum on Mennonite and Friends self-help projects
subfiles.from: RMH, Department of State
subfiles.about: Summarizes approval of a Mennonite community center in Japan and the probable approval of a similar Friends project.
subfiles.summary: Memo on a Mennonite Central Committee center offering sewing, shoe repair, reading and crafts, approved by headquarters as externally funded democratic welfare demonstration without religious implications; an American Friends Service Committee proposal expected.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 443: Approval of Foreign Rehabilitation and Self-Help Social Service Projects for Japan
subfiles.from: William J. Sebald, United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Reports SCAP's policy permitting externally supported rehabilitation and self-help social-service projects in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Despatch 443: after a Mennonite community-center proposal, approval of self-help projects requires secular social-service character, foreign support, no duplicate general relief and no special privileges; a similar Friends center in Tokyo is expected to be approved.

subfiles.title: SCAP press release on foreign social-work projects
subfiles.from: General Headquarters, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Announces conditions under which foreign organizations may establish modern social-service demonstration projects in Japan.
subfiles.summary: SCAP states that qualified, democratically operated welfare projects may train Japanese workers through direct participation. Sponsors must supply their own personnel and logistical needs, avoid general relief distribution and religious discrimination, comply with occupation rules, and expect no support from Japan's impoverished economy.

subfiles.title: American Red Cross inquiry about the Doai Foundation and earthquake hospitals
subfiles.from: Elizabeth Lindemann, American National Red Cross
subfiles.to: G. Bernard Noble, Department of State
subfiles.about: Requests an opinion on American interests in the Doai Foundation's remaining hospital assets.
subfiles.summary: Lindemann recounts American earthquake funds built Tokyo and Yokohama hospitals after 1923, run by the Doai Foundation until dissolved in wartime, and asks confirmation the Red Cross and U.S. government hold no control before approving SCAP's lease of Yokohama Memorial Hospital for municipal teaching.

subfiles.title: Reply on ownership and control of Doai Foundation assets
subfiles.from: G. Bernard Noble, Department of State
subfiles.to: Elizabeth Lindemann, American National Red Cross
subfiles.about: Concludes from 1924 diplomatic records that the Red Cross imposed no restrictions on Japan's use of its earthquake-relief funds.
subfiles.summary: Noble quotes Secretary Hughes's instructions that the U.S. government had no part in proposing a memorial hospital and the Red Cross wanted Japan to use funds as it saw fit, with the balance wholly at Japanese disposal, so no American control remains.
keywords: Foreign Relations of the United States

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 350: Request for Transmittal of a Resolution Adopted by the Japanese House of Representatives
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Forwards Japan's request to circulate a resolution thanking overseas Japanese communities for postwar relief.
subfiles.summary: Despatch 350: Japan's Foreign Ministry asks that a House resolution be brought to Japanese residents of the U.S., Hawaii, Canada, Cuba, Colombia, Venezuela and Argentina, and separately asked the Swedish mission to forward similar requests to other Latin American governments.

subfiles.title: Japanese Foreign Ministry note requesting transmission of the gratitude resolution
subfiles.from: I. Ohta, Japanese Ministry of Foreign Affairs
subfiles.to: General Headquarters, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Requests American assistance in conveying Japan's relief-gratitude resolution to Japanese communities in countries lacking Japanese representation.
subfiles.summary: Japan's Foreign Ministry encloses the House resolution in English, asking SCAP to use national authorities or U.S. diplomats to reach Japanese residents in the U.S., Canada, Cuba, Colombia, Venezuela and Argentina.

subfiles.title: Resolution thanking overseas Japanese for aid to Japan
subfiles.from: Japanese House of Representatives
subfiles.to: Japanese and citizens of Japanese parentage abroad
subfiles.about: Expresses formal gratitude for post-surrender relief supplied by Japanese communities in Hawaii and the Americas.
subfiles.summary: House resolution thanks overseas Japanese for LARA goods, CARE goods and relief parcels since the surrender, which gave consolation and encouragement.

subfiles.title: Letter forwarding the Japanese gratitude resolution to the Hawaii Times
subfiles.from: Max W. Bishop, Department of State
subfiles.about: Informally forwards the Japanese House of Representatives resolution for possible newspaper coverage.
subfiles.summary: Bishop sends the Hawaii Times a translation of Japan's resolution thanking Japanese abroad for relief parcels, suggesting it may wish to publicize it.

subfiles.title: Memorandum transmitting the gratitude resolution to Canada
subfiles.from: Department of State
subfiles.about: Transmits Japan's resolution thanking overseas Japanese for postwar relief.
subfiles.summary: Memo to Canada: at SCAP's request for Japan, the Department forwards the April 28 resolution, hoping it reaches Japanese and persons of Japanese parentage in the Western Hemisphere.

subfiles.title: Memorandum transmitting the gratitude resolution to Cuba
subfiles.from: Department of State
subfiles.about: Forwards the Japanese relief-gratitude resolution to Cuba for circulation among residents of Japanese origin.
subfiles.summary: Memo to Cuba: SCAP asked transmission since Cuba and some governments lack representation in Japan; the resolution thanks overseas Japanese for postwar relief.

subfiles.title: Enclosed translation of the Japanese gratitude resolution
subfiles.from: Japanese House of Representatives
subfiles.to: Japanese and citizens of Japanese parentage abroad
subfiles.about: Provides the translated resolution enclosed with diplomatic memoranda circulating Japan's thanks.
subfiles.summary: Translated resolution thanks Japanese communities in Hawaii and the Americas for LARA and CARE goods and relief parcels, which gave consolation and encouragement.

subfiles.title: Memorandum transmitting the gratitude resolution to Venezuela
subfiles.from: Department of State
subfiles.about: Forwards Japan's resolution of thanks for circulation among Japanese residents and people of Japanese origin in Venezuela.
subfiles.summary: Memo to Venezuela: the Department conveys the resolution at SCAP's request, as Japan wishes Western Hemisphere communities informed of its gratitude.

subfiles.title: Memorandum transmitting the gratitude resolution to Argentina
subfiles.from: Department of State
subfiles.about: Transmits Japan's resolution thanking Japanese residents abroad for relief parcels and other assistance.
subfiles.summary: Memo to Argentina forwards the translated April 28 resolution at SCAP's and Japan's request, for Japanese residents and persons of Japanese parentage.

subfiles.title: Cuban Embassy acknowledgment of the gratitude resolution
subfiles.from: Embassy of Cuba
subfiles.about: Acknowledges the American memorandum and agrees to forward Japan's gratitude resolution to Cuban authorities.
subfiles.summary: Cuban Embassy acknowledges the June 28 memorandum and resolution and will send it to Cuban authorities to inform Japanese residents.

subfiles.title: Colombian Embassy memorandum on forwarding the gratitude resolution
subfiles.from: Embassy of Colombia
subfiles.about: Reports that the Japanese gratitude resolution has been sent to Colombia's Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
subfiles.summary: Colombian Embassy acknowledges the translated resolution with the June 28 memorandum and says it was sent to Colombia's foreign ministry.

subfiles.title: Argentine Embassy acknowledgment of the gratitude resolution
subfiles.from: Embassy of the Argentine Republic
subfiles.about: Acknowledges the resolution and reports its referral to the Argentine government for notice to residents of Japanese ancestry.
subfiles.summary: Argentine Embassy acknowledges the June 28 memorandum and Japanese House resolution and says its government was informed to tell Japanese residents.

subfiles.title: Airgram A-314: Natural Resources Section Assumes Flood-Control Responsibility
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Transmits a GHQ announcement centralizing Japanese flood control, watershed management, reforestation, and hydrological planning.
subfiles.summary: Lieutenant Colonel Hubert G. Schenck links increasing flood damage to deforestation and cites major losses in transportation, reservoirs, farmland, housing, and human life. The Natural Resources Section proposes selective logging, rapid replanting, coordinated hydrological data collection, flood control, soil conservation, land reclamation, and study of water and hydroelectric resources.

subfiles.title: American Red Cross letter listing prisoner-of-war relief cargo
subfiles.from: Lawrence B. Libby, American Red Cross
subfiles.to: Eldred D. Kuppinger, Department of State
subfiles.about: Reports a large relief shipment sent from Portland through Vladivostok for delivery to prisoners of war in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Libby lists Red Cross food parcels, YMCA and Catholic recreational materials, blind-prisoner equipment, insurance forms and medical units shipped on the SS V Piateletka to the Red Cross delegate in Japan under separate bills of lading.

subfiles.title: Telegram on American Red Cross finances in Shanghai
subfiles.from: Josselyn, Shanghai, transmitting a message from Calvin
subfiles.to: Secretary of State; for O'Connor and Ryan, American Red Cross
subfiles.about: Reports American Red Cross cash, advances, expenditures, salary assignments, and currency conversions in a heavily garbled financial message.
subfiles.summary: Shanghai telegram on American Red Cross finances: nine advances totaling $4,028.12, salary assignments of $1,194.00, administrative spending, an India account credit, and $6,000 converted at about 1,579.

subfiles.title: Telegram announcing American Red Cross personnel departures for Shanghai
subfiles.from: James T. Nicholson, American Red Cross, through the Department of State
subfiles.about: Provides departure dates for three American Red Cross personnel traveling from San Francisco.
subfiles.summary: Telegram: Hyer left San Francisco by surface transport March 18; Nixon and Sexsmith are to leave March 23, per Ryan's American Red Cross message.
